title: Packed machine container representation
objective: Define reusable owner-bound packed sequence and matrix representation facts for optimizer domains, with length, element shape, alias, mutation, publication, cleanup, copy-cost, and resource proofs; implement isolated analysis/representation modules plus adversarial tests and benchmarks, but leave central registration and shared runtime hooks to integration.

handoff.summary: Implemented the standalone math.packed-machine-container-facts.v1 provider (domain packed-machine-container, priority 400) with JSON-safe source contracts for contiguous sequences and row/column-major matrices. The representation.owner-bound-packed-container.v1 plan is deeply frozen and records length/shape, canonical element layout, source/active/public ownership, affine byte-range alias relations, immutable versus transactional mutation, sealed publication, all-exit cleanup, exact maximum copy bytes, foreign-resource generation/open guards, provenance, invalidations, same-source fallback, and a deterministic fingerprint. verify.packed-machine-container.v1 independently recomputes every safety-critical fact and supports serialized detached replay. Tests cover read-only aliases, write rejection, copy-in/out, owner transfer, zero trips, interruption cleanup, malformed resources, overflow, accessors, post-analysis mutation, and twelve forged-plan classes. The benchmark separately reports plan/replay latency and measured 1 MiB borrow/copy and transactional transfer/copy boundary costs without claiming an executable target speedup.
risks: The provider is intentionally not registered in optimizer/catalog.ts or the lowering dispatcher, and no executable target consumes it on this lane.

Guarded maximum extents and owner/storage identities remain valid only until their recorded invalidation events; consuming passes must emit every listed guard before effects and include the plan fingerprint in cache identity.

Native and Wasm cleanup actions are declarative; a consuming target must execute close, transfer, and root-retention operations in the named allocator domain without exposing a raw address or mutable public array.

The complete pnpm test:integration command was attempted three times and stopped on the inherited test/dense-prime-host-boundary.cjs GF(2) scalar timing ratchet (50.093, 50.642, and 55.234 microseconds versus a 50 microsecond ceiling) under a shared host load around 13; that exact test passes in isolation and no lane file participates in it. The contract remains active until integration can record a clean receipt on an uncontended host.
next_steps: Integration should import packedContainerDomainPlugin from tools/python/optimizer/domains/packed-container/index.ts into an integration-owned representation-fact-provider registry using its exported id, domainId, priority, planningId, representationId, verifierId, factsProduced, analyze/requirePlan, and verify fields; it is not an executable AST pass and should not be placed in the current target-lowering catalog by itself.

A consuming modular, strict-binary64, fixed-extension, Wasm, or native pass should construct PackedContainerCandidate only after proving the complete live peer set, no callback, no escape, owner ancestry, exact guarded extents, canonical lane shape, and resource generation/open state; call requirePlan, immediately verify, attach the plan to its internal region, and verify again after any detached serialization.

The consuming emitter must map the stable packed-container.* guard codes and cleanup owner actions before optimized effects, preserve fallback.restart=original-inputs, publish only the sealed result owner, and own its target-specific lowering/emitter registration.
Rerun pnpm parallel:run -- optimizer-packed-containers -- pnpm test:integration on an uncontended host, then set status to review after parallel:check accepts the fresh passing receipt.
